newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty stable after dip, again eyes upside.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty stable after dip, again eyes upside.

text.p: The Polish zloty stabilised after losing half a point in early trade, but dealers said the market's week-long zloty-buying sentiment would soon return.
"The zloty fell in the morning and then stabilised. Now the buying trend is likely to return," said Karol Zaluski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said foreign investors remained inactive so far on Thursday after purchasing zlotys over the last few days and that the zloty's morning dip was mainly caused by speculation.
"It's the same scenario as yesterday, based on speculation by Polish banks," said Adam Roeske, dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.
At 0850 the zloty was at -1.50/-1.64 percent from the trading band centre against -1.02/-1.29 percent at opening.
It was at 3.4500/40 against the dollar, against 3.4360/80 at opening and at 1.8870/00 to the mark versus 1.8800/60.
Some said that small foreign-driven deals added to the zloty's stabilisation around 1.5 percent below parity in early trade with international players both buying and selling.
"There are clients from both sides...including foreigners mainly interested in zloty speculation," said Malgorzata Sawicka, forex dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said immediate official rate rise hopes subsided but that the central bank may increase market rates quickly in order to cool fast growing domestic demand.
Overnight rates eased to 21.90/22.10 percent from opening at 22.00/22.20 after a brief morning high around 22.80 at bid.
Tomorrow/next offers rose to 21.98/22.76 from 22.15/22.55 at opening after a 1.2 billion zloty drainage announcement.
Players were expected to test various levels at today's drainage and establish a new maximum rate after the central bank rejected all bids on Wednesday's reverse repo auctions.
